## Brief
The last bullet of "Failure signatures that are not your code" in
`.claude/skills/server-changes/SKILL.md` (line 141) reads:

    **`429` on `/otp` around the third consecutive full run** — the per-IP rate

Both halves are false, and they became false at different times.

The per-IP half died when `RUN_IP` landed: `test/server/functions.test.mjs`
gives every run its own `cf-connecting-ip`, so the per-IP buckets are run-scoped
and no longer accumulate (the long comment at `functions.test.mjs:80-101` is the
explanation, and `server/README.md` has the prose version).

The per-email half died on this branch's parent commit, BAD-067 (PR 383, merged):
`clearReviewerRateLimits()` in the same file deletes the `otp:REVIEWER_EMAIL`
and `activate:REVIEWER_EMAIL` rows from `private.rate_limits` at suite startup,
so the sixth-run 429 that this bullet was really describing is gone too.
`server/README.md` gained a paragraph about it.

The cost of leaving the line is precise: it teaches the next reader to shrug off
a 429 on `/otp` as a known local artefact, at exactly the moment a 429 there
became a real finding. That is the same dismissal BAD-067 was filed to end — it
cost two sessions an explanation apiece while the bullet said the failure was
nobody's code.

The judgement is what replaces it, and it is yours. Deleting the bullet outright
is one option and it is not obviously right: the section is a list of things that
are *not* your code, and a reader who hits a 429 now needs to be told the
opposite — that it is a finding, and what it means. The other bullets in that
section are the model for tone and length; match them, and match the file's
existing voice rather than importing one.

Weigh at least these:

- A 429 on `/otp` can still legitimately happen locally: the per-run IP bucket is
  10/hour and a single run spends about two, so a pathological loop inside one
  run could still trip it. Whether that is worth a line is your call.
- Whoever reads this section is mid-failure and scanning. Do not write a history

- If you conclude the honest thing is a line in a different section (a red flag,
